MODULATION

Some songs, especially jazz standards, move between two or more keys. Some even shift from major keys to minor keys, and vice versa, This transitioning of key centers is called modulation. Fig. 9 depicts a modulation from the key of C major to the key of Bb major. This sudden change of keys is called direct modulation. Using the key-center approach, you would play the C major scale for the first two measures, and the Bb major scale for measures 3-4.

Fig. 9

TRACK 30

Fig. 10 chord in G major. This is an example of pivot chord modulation. Am7 Is the pivot chord, or gateway chord, which provides a smooth transition from one key to the other. The key-center approach would be to play the A minor scale in the first half of the progression, and the G major scale in the second half. The pivot chord could receive either scale. The chaice is up to the soloist.

Fig. 10
